A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and added evaluations in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAE training experiments, RxRx1 and Anax linear probes, whole-genome RxRx3 benchmarks, and supplementary cell-condition and scaling analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds JUMP-CP evaluation, RxRx3-core compound–gene prediction, and microscopy DINO training experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed Phenoprints-16M curation procedure, MAE architectures and losses, and linear-probe selection of intermediate blocks remain unchanged. The newly reported DINO training attempts are comparison experiments, rather than changes to the proposed MAE method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on external JUMP-CP images covering 7,976 gene knockouts and introduces compound–gene activity prediction on RxRx3-core, containing 735 genetic knockouts and 1,674 compounds across eight concentrations. These extend both acquisition conditions and task requirements beyond v1's genetic-perturbation evaluations. Existing RxRx1, RxRx3 and Anax coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds CellProfiler comparisons on JUMP-CP and RxRx3-core, a random baseline for compound–gene prediction, and microscopy-trained DINO models, including an MAE initialized variant in Appendix A.9. It removes the ImageNet WSL ViT-L/16 comparator from the original whole-genome comparison. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparison approaches while changing membership in the retained benchmark.

E3.justification: Whole-genome recall changes from four database-specific columns to an aggregate over five databases, including Signor. New evaluations introduce PCA-based alignment, four-crop well averaging, concentration-dependent compound–gene ranking, and exclusion of 4,749 wells lacking CellProfiler features for all RxRx3-core models. Original MAE training budgets and probing settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 still lists only the original four relationship databases.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit generalization test across laboratories and assay protocols, examines trimming and compound concentration in the new prediction task, and diagnoses unsuccessful DINO training through loss curves and scratch-versus-fine-tuning results (Figure 7 and Table 6). The original Anax cell-condition checks and FLOP correlations are retained, with the latter moved from Appendix A.9 to A.10.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's existing permutation and replicate-consistency tests, v2 introduces mean and standard deviation over three null-sampling seeds for whole-genome recall, uncertainty reporting for JUMP-CP, and standard deviations and error bars over 100 benchmark seeds for RxRx3-core. It also reports improvement z-scores. These quantify benchmark sampling variability; they do not establish repeated model training.

E6.justification: v2 replaces database-specific whole-genome table entries with aggregate recall and adds substantial new results. JUMP-CP StringDB recall is 0.235 for trimmed MAE-G/8 versus 0.191 for CellProfiler; RxRx3-core mean average precision is 0.309 ± 0.015 for trimmed MAE-G/8 versus 0.290 ± 0.017 for the previous MAE-L/8. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over corresponding v1 experiments. The stated 42% gain concerns z-scores, 3.77 to 5.38. Original probing and KS/CVM results are largely retained.

T1.justification: The block-selection definition and perturbation-consistency, permutation-p-value, KS and CVM equations remain unchanged. v2 adds no original theorem, proof or substantive derivation; its discussion of MAE–contrastive relationships cites existing work.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain curated training data, a scaled MAE-G/8, and intermediate-block selection through biological probes. v2 extends the abstract's best-performance claim to compound–gene activity prediction and emphasizes efficient use of experimental data, while preserving the original methodological contribution and scaling claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning unsuccessful DINO training, the resulting allocation of compute to MAEs, and the unresolved potential of other SSL and fine-tuning recipes. It attributes lower external-data recall to assay differences and variability, and interprets continued MAE reconstruction-loss improvement as suggesting further scaling potential. These materially expand the interpretation and qualification of the findings.

D1.justification: v2 announces inference, visualization and benchmarking code plus CA-MAE-S/16 weights, and supplies RxRx3-core access information. Appendices A.9 and A.11 add DINO hyperparameters and CellProfiler extraction, aggregation and missing-data details. Existing MAE hyperparameters are retained. Some disclosure remains inconsistent: Section 6 calls the baseline CellProfiler 4, whereas A.11 specifies version 2.2.0.

R1.justification: The principal positioning relative to Kraus, Celik and intermediate-layer research remains intact. v2 adds contextual references on language-model data curation, mechanistic interpretability, alternative SSL/fine-tuning approaches, CellProfiler and RxRx3-core, while removing some broad biological foundation-model background. This updates and extends the context without fundamentally redefining the claimed relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around data efficiency, replacing the original contribution bullets with a developed narrative. Related-work topics are reordered, the discussion is expanded, and dedicated external-evaluation, compound–gene benchmarking, limitations/reproducibility and impact sections restructure the paper.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, moves the model inventory into the appendix, restructures the whole-genome table, and adds benchmark tables, a concentration plot and a DINO loss plot. The original replicate-similarity distribution figure is removed, while retained figures are resized or relocated. Figure 1's caption loses its detailed model-to-bar mapping and ends after introducing that mapping.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's lack of validation on data from other laboratories and direct compound–gene prediction. JUMP-CP and RxRx3-core results, additional comparison methods, sampling uncertainty and documented DINO failures make the conclusions better supported; code and small-model access information also improves reproducibility. Aggregate recall loses database-level detail, and the 42% wording requires qualification as a z-score comparison, but these reporting weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
